title: Accessible Modals & Dialogs 🔔
description: Craft a modal dialog with focus trapping, labelledby, and proper semantics.

slides.title: The Dialog Role 🪟
slides.content:
A modal dialog is a window that overlays the page and demands user interaction.

* `role="dialog"` or the `<dialog>` element (preferred, with JavaScript).
* `aria-modal="true"` indicates that content behind is inert.
* Must have an accessible name (`aria-labelledby` pointing to the title).
* Must trap focus: pressing Tab at the last element wraps to the first; Shift+Tab at the first wraps to the last.
* When closed, focus must return to the trigger element.

quizData.question: What does `aria-modal="true"` on a dialog achieve?

options.text: It makes the dialog visually modal
It tells assistive tech that content outside the dialog should be ignored

quizData.explanation: It signals to screen readers that only the dialog content is available; you still must manage focus trapping with JavaScript.

slides.title: Focus Trapping 🔒
slides.content:
While the dialog is open:

* All focusable elements outside the dialog must be unfocusable (set `tabindex="-1"` or use `inert` attribute).
* A focus trap script listens for Tab/Shift+Tab and loops within the dialog's focusable elements.

Modern browsers support the `inert` attribute; you can apply `inert` to the main content behind the dialog.

quizData.question: What should happen when a modal closes?

options.text: Focus goes to the next focusable element on the page
Focus returns to the element that triggered the dialog

quizData.explanation: Restoring focus to the trigger preserves context and continuity for keyboard and screen reader users.

slides.title: The `<dialog>` Element ✨
slides.content:
HTML `<dialog>` has built‑in methods:

* `dialog.showModal()` opens it modally, adds backdrop, and traps focus natively (in modern browsers).
* Still need `aria-labelledby` for the accessible name.
* Use `<form method="dialog">` inside to close with Enter.

Prefer `<dialog>` over div‑based approaches – less JavaScript, better semantics.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Escape Key Handling
Dialogs must close on Escape. The native `<dialog>` does this automatically. For custom dialogs, listen for `keydown` on Escape.
